subject: micro_ncep; Warning messages relating to GDAL/PROJ development?

messages.author: d9c7d6ab90c62b6b
messages.subject: micro_ncep; Warning messages relating to GDAL/PROJ development?
parts:
Hi all,

After a considerable hiatus from working with NicheMapR I recently updated R (to 4.0.2) and my packages. I'm now receiving warning messages (pasted below) that appear related to GDAL/PROJ development (https://www.r-spatial.org/r/2020/03/17/wkt.html). After some reading up over the last few days i'm still unsure of how worried or otherwise I should be about them?

I'd be grateful for any advise.

Take care,

Tom

For reference:
I'm running the example code from the micro_ncep vignette as a test run, with most recent version of NicheMapR from github.

dstart <- "02/01/2017" 
dfinish <- "30/12/2017" 
loc <- c(-91.415669, -0.287145) # Isla Fernandina Galapagos 
micro<-micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)  

Warning messages:
1: In showSRID(uprojargs, format = "PROJ", multiline = "NO") :
  Discarded ellps WGS 84 in CRS definition: +proj=merc +a=6378137 +b=6378137 +lat_ts=0 +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +k=1 +units=m +nadgrids=@null +wktext +no_defs
2: In showSRID(uprojargs, format = "PROJ", multiline = "NO") :
  Discarded datum WGS_1984 in CRS definition
...
25: In if (class(r) == "RasterLayer") r <- getValues(r, format = "matrix") :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
...

messages.author: d9c7d6ab90c62b6b
messages.subject: Re: micro_ncep; Warning messages relating to GDAL/PROJ development?
parts:
To update, in case an issue with my packages I entirely removed R, RStudio and my package libraries and re-installed from scratch. This led to the same warnings, suggesting to me that this could be something that could start popping up for others once packages/R is updated. 

From what I can see so far it depends on how CRS are handled.

https://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/372692/how-should-i-handle-crs-properly-after-the-major-change-in-proj-library

I'll have a go at further googling (though not familiar with spatial R) and report back if I can shed any light on it. 

Take care,

Tom
